newsitem.title: UK: Poor profits push East West Insurance into run-off.
newsitem.headline: Poor profits push East West Insurance into run-off.

text.p: UK-based East West Insurance has ceased all underwriting with immediate effect and put its business into run-off, the company said in a statement on Tuesday.
"The fierce competition prevalent within the UK insurance sector has prohibited the company from providing reasonable expectation of an appropriate return to its shareholders," the statement said.
"It is with regret therefore, that we must announce that the board have agreed to cease with immediate effect all underwriting activity and withdraw from the UK insurance market."
The firm, based in Gloucester, operated in motor, personal accident, property and liability business using brokers for distribution.
The company invested in electronic systems in a bid to allow its brokers to compete with the big insurance companies and direct telephone-based firms.
However, recently it had to fend off criticism from some brokers that it had been trying to bypass them and deal direct with customers.
The decision to cease trading was made "despite the advantages of electronic data interchange and the support of the broker community".
"It must be stressed the decision is strategic and is not dictated by the current asset levels of the company which meet solvency requirements," the statement said.

East West said it would continue to administer existing policies and claims until they have expired. Lloyd's underwriting operation Equity Red Star will take on East West's portfolio and offer to renew policies.
